## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 495) is a verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past karmic deeds and verse narrative of the elder (*thera*) Koraṇḍapupphiya [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists five translations across five different languages for the text, though it provides no standalone English title [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 99 matching passages across 38 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The text exhibits near-verbatim duplication across its entire span (§0.2–12.1, similarity 0.99) with an earlier, identically titled apadāna, *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 427) [DharmaNexus]. Passages from its opening verses (§1.3–5.3) are likewise shared with the first volume of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Standard repetitive stock verses, particularly spanning §7.1–12.1, are shared with numerous other *Therāpadāna* poems, including *Upaḍḍhadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 497), *Ekadīpiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 418), *Naḷakuṭidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 501), and *Kiṁsukapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 496) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several short segments with the Tibetan *Karmaśataka* (D0340) with a low plausibility score of 10, but SuttaCentral does not recognize any curated cross-language parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
